## Course identity

This repository contains the public teaching material for a practical workshop on reproducible analysis of public RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data using small genomes and personal laptops.

Author and maintainer: **Francesco Gualdrini**.

Public GitHub repository:

[https://github.com/fgualdr/Reproducible_NGS_Workshop](https://github.com/fgualdr/Reproducible_NGS_Workshop)

Published course website:

[https://fgualdr.github.io/Reproducible_NGS_Workshop/](https://fgualdr.github.io/Reproducible_NGS_Workshop/)

Students do **not** clone a finished analysis repository. They progressively create their own GitHub repositories, adding metadata, scripts, reports, figures, checkpoints, and interpretation as the course develops.

:::{.callout-important}
The teaching logic is:

```text
metadata -> scripts/commands -> outputs/results/reports/interpretation -> Git commit 
```

The execution backend may change, but the reproducibility logic should not.
:::

## Source plan

The workshop is intended to provide basic concept on reproducibility in bioinformatics and its link to FAIR science in addition to standard workflow in data retrival and RNA-seq and Chip-seq analysis.
Personal computer will be setup in order to use Git with an associated Github account and a Github repository which will grow during the workshop.
Containarized images will be generated with Podman (or Docker) and stored under personal DockerHub (which is free for accademic use with unlimited space).
VSCode will be the main IDE through which we will write-codes and deploy command in the terminal.

## Course schedule

| Session | Timing | Main focus |
|---|---:|---|
| Day 0 | before course | Installation, accounts, laptop-spec form, container smoke test |
| Day 1 | 4 h | Project setup, Git/GitHub, containers, public data retrieval, reference genome, a first FASTQC |
| Day 2 | 4 h | RNA-seq QC, trimming, mapping, counting, tracks, DESeq2 |
| Day 3 | 4 h | ChIP-seq QC, trimming, mapping, peak calling, tracks, motifs |
| Day 4 | 4 h | RNA-seq/ChIP-seq integration, visualization, discussion, final slides |

## Execution routes

1. Full local execution in Docker or Podman.
2. Partial local execution plus checkpoint files.
3. Downstream-only checkpoint mode using count matrices, peak files, bigWigs, QC reports, and annotation.

:::{.callout-warning}
Containers solve software installation. They do not solve weak hardware, limited disk, or unstable internet. Alternative checkpoints will be provided in case selected point will fail.
:::

## Repository map

- `days/`: day-by-day Quarto lessons.
- `modules/`: reusable conceptual modules.
- `backends/`: local, Codespaces, Galaxy, instructor-machine, and checkpoint routes.
- `scripts/`: instructor examples and student-copyable workflow templates.
- `student_repo_template/`: simple starter repository layout students copy into their own GitHub repositories (will be covered during the workshop)
- `config/`: example metadata and dataset candidate configuration.
- `containers/`: Docker/Podman and devcontainer material.
- `checkpoints/`: manifests and documentation for distributed fallback files.
- `assessments/`: rubrics and submission checklists.
- `instructor/`: course administration notes, not part of the main public teaching path.

## Student repository model

During the workshop each student creates a separate GitHub repository with:

```text
README.md
code/
container/
data/
results/
```

The `README.md` is the main reproducibility record. The `data/` directory exists locally but large sequencing and alignment files are ignored by Git through .gitignore specs.
